name: Aphiah
overview: Aphiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the father of Becorath and an ancestor of King Saul. His role in Scripture is brief but significant due to his genealogical connection within the lineage of Israel's first king. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Aphiah appears only once in Scripture and does not have a recorded meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Aphiah as the father of Becorath and a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin. These relationships establish his place within the genealogical line leading to King Saul. Beyond this, no other family connections are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Aphiah’s significance lies in his position within the ancestral line of King Saul, Israel's first monarch. As the father of Becorath, he connects the tribe of Benjamin to the royal lineage, underscoring the biblical emphasis on tribal heritage and divine appointment in leadership. His mention in 1 Samuel 9:1 situates him within the historical context that leads to Saul’s rise as king.
